panels.title: Tokens / h by type
panels.description: From Claude Code's own api_request events in Loki (ADR-014), one per model request. Present only for sessions with Claude Code's telemetry on (`stdtel-install settings`, or `--native-only` with the plugin): a session without it is missing here, not free. Cache reads usually dominate; compare the other three with each other. Cache reads are on the right axis: they are usually 100x the rest.

panels.title: Spend by skill, agent and repo (in range)
panels.description: From Claude Code's own api_request events in Loki (ADR-014), one per model request. Present only for sessions with Claude Code's telemetry on (`stdtel-install settings`, or `--native-only` with the plugin): a session without it is missing here, not free. `(no skill)` is spend outside any skill, usually most of it. A third-party plugin's skill reads `third-party` unless the detailed view is on; the warehouse's llm_request_attributed names it where stdtel saw exactly one run in that prompt.

targets.expr: sum by (skill_name, agent_name, vcs_repository_name) (sum_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name="api_request" | label_format skill_name=`{{ or .skill_name "(no skill)" }}`, agent_name=`{{ or .agent_name "(main)" }}` | unwrap cost_usd [$__range]))

panels.title: MCP calls by server and tool (in range)
panels.description: From Claude Code's own tool_result events in Loki (ADR-014). Present only for sessions with Claude Code's telemetry on (`stdtel-install settings`, or `--native-only` with the plugin). MCP server and tool names, and the skill a Skill call loaded, arrive only with the detailed view on (`stdtel-install detailed-view on`, via the stdtel-setup skill); without it they read `(hidden: detailed view off)`. The collector keeps those names and drops everything else in the call (#142).

targets.expr: sum by (mcp_server_name, mcp_tool_name) (count_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name="tool_result" | tool_name="mcp_tool" | label_format mcp_server_name=`{{ or .mcp_server_name "(hidden: detailed view off)" }}`, mcp_tool_name=`{{ or .mcp_tool_name "-" }}` [$__range]))

defaults.noValue: No MCP call in this range

panels.title: Skills invoked (in range)
panels.description: From Claude Code's own tool_result events in Loki (ADR-014). Present only for sessions with Claude Code's telemetry on (`stdtel-install settings`, or `--native-only` with the plugin). MCP server and tool names, and the skill a Skill call loaded, arrive only with the detailed view on (`stdtel-install detailed-view on`, via the stdtel-setup skill); without it they read `(hidden: detailed view off)`. The collector keeps those names and drops everything else in the call (#142). Counts Skill tool calls in the range, so a long loop started earlier does not appear.

targets.expr: sum by (skill_name) (count_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name="tool_result" | tool_name="Skill" | label_format skill_name=`{{ or .skill_name "(hidden: detailed view off)" }}` [$__range]))

defaults.noValue: No skill ran in this range

panels.title: Activations / h by artefact kind
panels.description: Where the agent's work actually goes. Sub-agents and compaction were invisible before ADR-009; a session can have no skill activations at all and still be the most expensive one of the day.

panels.title: Sub-agent calls / h by type
panels.description: Rate only — a sub-agent's token cost is a span attribute, so read that from the warehouse (warehouse/efficiency/), not from here.

panels.title: p50 hook-observed turn duration
panels.description: The harness's own turn timing, not our clock.

panels.title: Compactions / h by reason
panels.description: A rising auto-compaction rate is context pressure: the session is spending tokens re-reading itself. Pair with tokens_before in the warehouse.

panels.title: External spend calls / h by system
panels.description: ADR-010 decision 7. Spend that happens outside the harness, reported by whatever spent it — a CLI the agent shells out to, or an MCP server calling models of its own. stdtel cannot observe this; it receives it, so an empty graph means either nothing ran or nothing is emitting, and those are different. The money is not here: cost is a Postgres figure, on the outcomes board.

description: Invocation rate, errors, duration and token flow. The scorecard — first-time policy pass rate and the keep/refine/deprecate call — is on 'Skill scorecard'.
